text.p: Colombia's main airline Avianca will spend more than $8.5 million in the next five months to improve infrastructure and promote tourism to the country, a company spokeswoman said Tuesday.
The spokeswoman said $6 million will be spent to modernize facilities and equipemnt, though not its fleet of aircraft. The remainder will be spent on security and a tourism promotion campaign.
Avianca has signed a deal with the country's major hotel chains and will announce a series of cut-rate package vacations August 23, she said.
The airline is also awaiting U.S. government approval of a December "reservation-sharing" deal with American Airlines.
The deal allows Avianca -- which only has landing rights at Miami, New York and Los Angeles -- to book its passengers on American Airlines connecting flights to most U.S. destinations.
